newsitem.title: DENMARK: FOCUS-Danisco 96/97 profits up, but forecast sours.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Danisco 96/97 profits up, but forecast sours.

text.p: Danish sugar, spirits and packaging group Danisco on Wednesday announced 1996/1997 profits 14 percent up on the year before but forecast a slower growth rate for next year.
The outlook disappointed the stock market and sent the Danisco share down an intitial four percent, at the same time slowing a recovery of the KFX top 20 shares index.

Danisco reported consolidated profits up to 1.392 billion crowns ($211.8 million) in 1996/97, from 1.218 billion the year before, on a turnover of 17.00 billion crowns, five percent up on its 16.18 billion in 1995/96.
"For the accounting year 1997/98 an improved group result is expected. The rise, however, is expected to be less than in 1996/97," Danisco said in its report.

It logged rises in sales and profits in its food and beverage, sugar and packaging divisions but said the sharpest rises -- 12 percent on sales and 20 percent on operating profit -- came in its ingredients operation, which makes flavourings, stabilisers and other ingredients for the food industry.
The group raised its dividend to five crowns per 20 crown share from last year's 4.20 but failed to outweigh the stock market's disappointment with its growth forecast.
Around midday the share was down to 416.00 crowns, from 432.00 before the results were published.
"It is the expectations that are disappointing, absolutely. The 1996/97 accounts were as expected," a dealer said.

Traders said that Danisco's fall helped put the brakes on the KFX top 20 share index, which had been following Wall Street's recovery but fell from a high of 172.80 to 172.24 after the Danisco report, 0.04 point below Tuesday's close. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650 ($ = 6.571 Danish Crowns)
